verdict: C.H. Robinson's revenue jumped 29.5% to $5,358M on higher freight pricing, and leaner operations turned that into a 22% rise in profit to $198M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $1.34 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.80

kpis.label: Adjusted gross profit
kpis.note: up 14.5% — what is left after paying carriers

segments.name: North American Surface Transportation
segments.note: Truckload and less-than-truckload (LTL — sharing truck space) freight across North America. Revenue up 29.1% on higher pricing and 3.5% higher volume; adjusted gross profit per truckload shipment rose 17%.

segments.name: Global Forwarding
segments.note: Ocean and air freight forwarding around the world. Revenue up 46.1% on higher ocean and air pricing; operating income rose 63% to $80M.

segments.name: All Other and Corporate
segments.note: Mainly Robinson Fresh — sourcing and reselling fresh produce — plus corporate items. Revenue was roughly flat, down about 1%.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay for its people — up 3.1% on higher incentive pay for strong results, even as average headcount fell 10.4%.

opex.name: Other SG&A
opex.note: Other selling, general and administrative costs — up 29.7% on higher claims expenses and a lease impairment charge in Kansas City.

otherDetail: Interest and other expense, net was $22M: about $20M of interest expense on a higher average debt balance, plus a $2M net foreign-currency loss.
oneTimers: Results include $19M of specified items the company strips out of its adjusted figures — severance and other personnel costs, plus other SG&A items including an impairment charge on the Kansas City regional center lease after subleasing the remaining space. Adjusted operating income was $291M vs $272M GAAP, and adjusted EPS was $1.80 vs $1.67.
footerNote: C.H. Robinson is asset-light: it buys transportation from carriers and resells it. Following the company's own presentation, purchased transportation ($4,237M) plus purchased products sourced for resale ($313M) are shown as the direct-cost block, so gross profit here is the company's adjusted gross profit of $808M (reported gross profit of $796M also deducts $13M of software amortization). Figures are rounded to $M.

takeaways.title: Pricing drove the top line
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $5,358M as truckload, ocean, LTL and air pricing all rose and truckload volume grew. North American Surface Transportation — 71% of revenue — grew 29%, and Global Forwarding grew 46%.

takeaways.title: Each load earned more
takeaways.text: Adjusted gross profit — what Robinson keeps after paying carriers — rose 14.5% to $808M. Truckload adjusted gross profit per shipment rose 17% as disciplined repricing outran a 33.5% rise in linehaul cost per mile.

takeaways.title: More freight, fewer people
takeaways.text: Average headcount fell 10.4% while volume grew, as manual processes were turned into automated, AI-assisted workflows. Operating income rose 23% to $272M and net income rose 22% to $198M.
